sets.title: Vocabulary · everyday words (set 4)
sets.instruction: Choose the word that fits the sentence best.

questions.q: The old gate was so __________ that it fell off when I pushed it.
questions.tip: 'Rusty' metal is weak and crumbling, which is why the gate fell off.

questions.q: Grandfather walked slowly because he was __________ after the long journey.
The kitten was too __________ to come out from under the sofa.
questions.tip: 'Timid' means easily frightened, which explains why it stayed hidden.

questions.q: Mother told us to speak in a __________ so that we would not wake the baby.
The floor was __________ after the mopping, so we walked carefully.
questions.tip: 'Damp' means slightly wet, which is how a freshly mopped floor feels.

questions.q: Ravi __________ down the corridor so that nobody would hear him.
questions.tip: To 'tiptoe' is to walk on your toes, very quietly.

questions.q: The glue made my fingers __________.
questions.tip: 'Sticky' things hold on to your skin, which glue does.

questions.q: We could not swim at that end because the water was too __________.
questions.tip: 'Shallow' water is not deep, so there is no room to swim.

questions.q: The wind was so __________ that it bent the young trees.
Siti was __________ about what was inside the parcel.
Please __________ the towel neatly before you put it away.
questions.tip: To 'fold' something is to bend it over so it lies flat and neat.

questions.q: The branch __________ in half when the boy sat on it.
questions.tip: To 'snap' is to break suddenly with a sharp sound.

questions.q: I had to __________ the lemon hard to get any juice out.
questions.tip: To 'squeeze' is to press something tightly.

questions.q: My little brother __________ across the floor before he could walk.
questions.tip: Babies 'crawl' on their hands and knees.

questions.q: The sky grew __________ and we knew the rain was coming.
Uncle Lim is very __________ with children who ask many questions.
questions.tip: A 'patient' person does not get annoyed by waiting or by questions.

questions.q: The boy was __________ and refused to apologise.
questions.tip: A 'stubborn' person will not change his mind.

questions.q: Leaves were __________ all over the playground after the storm.
I felt __________ before I went up to read in front of the school.
questions.tip: 'Nervous' means worried and a little afraid.

questions.q: The cat __________ out in the sun and closed its eyes.
questions.tip: To 'stretch' is to make your body longer and looser.

questions.q: Nobody wanted to sit on the __________ chair in the corner.
questions.tip: A 'wobbly' chair is not steady, so it is not safe to sit on.

questions.q: The boys had to __________ the heavy box across the floor.
questions.tip: To 'drag' is to pull something along the ground because it is too heavy to carry.

questions.q: Please do not __________ your classmates in the queue.
We were __________ with mud after the obstacle course.
questions.tip: 'Covered with' mud means mud was all over us.

questions.q: The puppy __________ when it heard the thunder.
questions.tip: To 'tremble' is to shake because you are afraid or cold.

questions.q: The girls __________ behind their hands at the teacher's joke.
questions.tip: To 'giggle' is to laugh in a small, quiet way.

questions.q: Arun __________ his answer so softly that nobody heard it.
questions.tip: To 'mumble' is to speak unclearly and too quietly.

questions.q: Mother __________ when she saw the state of my room.
questions.tip: To 'sigh' is to let out a long breath, often when you are tired or disappointed.

questions.q: The path up the hill was narrow and __________.
We kept a __________ key under the flowerpot.
questions.tip: A 'spare' key is an extra one, kept in case it is needed.

questions.q: The tiny lamp __________ in the dark corridor.
questions.tip: To 'glow' is to give out a soft, steady light.

questions.q: The candle flame __________ whenever the fan turned.
questions.tip: To 'flicker' is to burn unsteadily, going bright and dim.

questions.q: By four o'clock the writing on the board had almost __________.
questions.tip: To 'fade' is to become fainter and harder to see.

questions.q: The temple was __________ — it was built hundreds of years ago.
An __________ crowd waited outside the stadium.
Please keep your desk __________ so that you can find things.
Mei Qi felt __________ on her first day, before she made any friends.
questions.tip: 'Lonely' means unhappy because you are alone.

questions.q: Hari was __________ when his brother won the prize he had wanted.
questions.tip: 'Jealous' means unhappy because somebody else has what you want.

questions.q: It is __________ to say 'please' and 'thank you'.
The old man __________ about the noise from the flat above.
questions.tip: To 'grumble' is to complain in a low, unhappy voice.

questions.q: The girls __________ all the way home about the school trip.
questions.tip: To 'chatter' is to talk quickly and happily for a long time.

questions.q: Father __________ so loudly last night that I could hear him through the wall.
questions.tip: To 'snore' is to breathe noisily while you are asleep.

questions.q: I __________ to the shop because there was no hurry.
questions.tip: To 'stroll' is to walk slowly and in a relaxed way.

questions.q: Ben __________ for the bus and only just caught it.
questions.tip: To 'dash' is to run very fast for a short distance.

questions.q: After twisting his ankle, Rahim __________ off the field.
questions.tip: To 'limp' is to walk unevenly because one leg hurts.

questions.q: We __________ through the market with no particular plan.
questions.tip: To 'wander' is to walk about without aiming for anywhere.

questions.q: The fisherman __________ the net into the sea.
questions.tip: To 'toss' is to throw something lightly.

questions.q: Please __________ the rope — I cannot hold it any longer.
questions.tip: To 'release' something is to let go of it.

questions.q: A thin layer of frost made the glass __________.
questions.tip: 'Blurred' means not clear, so you cannot see through it properly.

questions.q: The dew on the grass __________ in the morning sun.
questions.tip: To 'sparkle' is to shine with many small flashes of light.

sets.title: Vocabulary cloze · two short passages
sets.instruction: Fill each blank with one suitable word. More than one word may fit; the mark scheme lists the ones that are accepted.

passages.text:
Passage A — The School Fish Tank

The fish tank stands beside the library door, and every Primary 3 class takes a (1)______ at looking after it.

Last term it was our job. Mrs Devi showed us how much food to give: one small (2)______ each morning, and no more, because the leftover food makes the water (3)______.

On Tuesday we noticed that one of the orange fish was swimming on its side. We told Mrs Devi at once, and she said we had done the right thing to (4)______ it so quickly.

She moved it into a smaller tank of its own. Three days later it was (5)______ again, and we put it back with the others.

Passage B — The Rainy Morning

The rain started before six o'clock and did not stop. By the time I reached the bus stop my shoes were (6)______ through.

There was already a long (7)______ of people waiting, and no shelter at all for the last ten of us.

Then a lady in a yellow raincoat (8)______ her umbrella over the smallest children so that they would stay dry. Nobody had asked her to.

When the bus finally came, everybody climbed on (9)______ and nobody pushed.

I was fifteen minutes late for school, but Mr Siva said he would (10)______ me, because half the class was late as well.

answers.tip: Each class 'takes a turn' — they do it one after another.
A very small amount of fish food is a 'pinch' — or a 'spoonful' or 'scoop'.
Leftover food rots, so the water becomes 'dirty' or 'cloudy'.
They told her quickly, so what they did quickly was 'notice' or 'report' it.
The fish recovered, so it was 'well' or 'healthy' again.
The rain went right through them, so they were 'soaked' through.
People waiting one behind another form a 'queue'.
She 'held' her umbrella over them — the past tense is needed.
'Nobody pushed' tells you they boarded 'calmly' or 'quietly'.
He would let it pass, so he would 'excuse' or 'forgive' her.
